Lena, Aditya — summary of the dedicated-GPU isolation model and eviction behavior (concise, auditor-friendly):

1) KV/prefix cache isolation
- Our Dedicated offering assigns tenant workloads to isolated GPU hosts or to pinned GPU instances within a reserved pool. KV caches and caches derived from prefix tokens are process-isolated: each tenant is served by processes/containers scoped to that tenant; internal runtime enforces per-tenant cache namespaces and keys. There are no shared on-disk cache artifacts between tenants.

2) GPU scheduling and noisy-neighbor mitigation
- We primarily use host-level isolation for Dedicated pools (no mixed-tenant CUDA processes on the same GPU). For customers requiring narrower blast radius, we can provision MIG where supported to carve physical GPU into isolated instances.
- When workloads are colocated in a burst/oversubscribe scenario, the runtime uses enforced cgroup constraints and our scheduler to cap GPU utilization per tenant; we also have an autoscaling/burst policy that can migrate load to other nodes rather than best-effort oversubscription in steady state.

3) Eviction and degradation behavior
- Eviction is deterministic: if host-level resource pressure requires reclaim, the runtime will gracefully drain new requests for the affected tenant and optionally failover to a compatible model variant in another pool (smaller quantized model) depending on your rollback policy. We do not perform silent truncation of ongoing token streams; either the request completes as issued or returns an explicit error/fallback response.

4) Evidence and artifacts we can provide
- Redacted SOC 2 Type II report (control mapped).
- SIG spreadsheet with our answers and control references.
- Short isolation diagram (attached).
- Sample runtime logs showing per-tenant cache namespaces and eviction events (we can provide redacted extracts).

Attachment: [Attachment: isolation_diagram.png (image/png)]

If you want a tightly worded procurement attestation paragraph, suggest wording below and we can sign off: 

"Redwood Inference confirms that in Dedicated deployments tenant runtime processes and key-value caches are namespace-separated. Under normal Dedicated allocations, tenant workloads are not allowed to access another tenant's in-memory KV cache or persisted cache artifacts. For customers choosing GPU carve-outs (MIG), hardware-level partitioning further reduces blast radius."

Happy to adapt wording for your legal team.

— Priyom
